description: Many tourists who come to Goa are satisfied with lounging on its picturesque white sandy beaches, occasionally taking a dip in the ocean or pool to acquire a sun-kissed tan. Nevertheless, Goa offers more than just its coastal attractions. One of its most captivating features lies within its abundant wildlife sanctuaries. These natural havens have gained popularity among enthusiasts of animals, birds, and nature alike. Among these sanctuaries, the Cotigao Wildlife Sanctuary stands out as the second largest and most accessible (open year-round) option. It is located in the southern part of Goa, along the Goa-Karnataka border. While visitors may not frequently encounter larger animals, the sanctuary's lush trees and vibrant avian species make it a favored destination for the adventurous traveller. WHERE TO VISIT Situated in the Canacona Taluka of South Goa, near the Goa-Karnataka border, this sanctuary makes for a delightful day trip from Palolem Beach. For those seeking a longer stay, accommodations can be arranged through the Forest Department with prior permission. TOP EXPERIENCES One of the notable attractions in this sanctuary is an observation deck cleverly concealed within the foliage of a 25-meter tall tree. This platform provides intrepid explorers an unobstructed view of the watering hole, where animals gather at dawn and dusk to quench their thirst. HISTORICAL BACKGROUND AND DESCRIPTION Established in 1968, the Cotigao Wildlife Sanctuary was created to safeguard the exposed woodland along the Goa-Karnataka border. This area was home to various animal and bird species, along with some rare, ancient trees. Spanning 86 square kilometers, the sanctuary boasts impressively tall trees, some reaching heights of 30 meters, casting shadows that cover the forest floor. The vegetation consists mainly of moist-deciduous types, interspersed with semi-evergreen and evergreen patches. WILDLIFE WITHIN THE SANCTUARY While tigers and leopards have left the region, other fascinating creatures inhabit the sanctuary. Visitors might catch glimpses of flying squirrels, slender lorises, Indian pangolins, mouse deer, four-horned antelopes, various snake species, and an array of colorful birds. Keen observers might even spot elusive residents like Gazelles, Sloth Bears, Porcupines, Panthers, and Hyenas, although these creatures tend to stay within the densest underbrush. Additional Attractions Beyond its rich vegetation and avian diversity, the sanctuary offers more attractions: Nature Interpretation Centre: A valuable resource for visitors curious about the flora and fauna within the sanctuary. Hiking Trails: For the more energetic, the sanctuary provides eight trails, ranging from 500 meters to 5 kilometers in length. Treetop Perches: A unique experience offered by the sanctuary, allowing visitors to view animal-frequented watering holes from six different lookout towers, each positioned at least 25 meters above ground level. Interaction with Tribal Peoples: The sanctuary is also home to ancient tribes like the Velip and Kunbil. Engaging with these indigenous communities provides insights into their culture and way of life. A visit to a sanctuary like Cotigao instills a sense of wonder for nature's marvels and its ability to cater to all living beings. Regardless of the time of year chosen for a visit, expect a tranquil and rejuvenating day in the midst of nature, enriched by physical activities and mental exploration

Opening Hours: The sanctuary is open to visitors every day from 7:00 AM to 5:30 PM.
Entrance Fees: The cost of admission is Rs. 5 per person. Additionally, there is a Rs. 25 fee for those carrying cameras.
Overnight Stays: Visitors wishing to stay overnight should obtain permission from the Deputy Conservator of Forests in Margao. The Forest Department provides various accommodations, including cots and mosquito nets for the adventurous, as well as canvas tents and snake-proof campsites for those interested.
Seasonal Considerations: While the prime tourist season typically runs from October to March, visiting during the monsoon season offers its advantages. The copious rainfall cleanses the environment and results in abundant greenery throughout the area.
